title: Evaluating an Astronomy-Inspired Colour–Colour Diagram Approach for River Turbidity Assessment: Implications for Arsenic Contamination Screening in the Kok and Sai Rivers, Thailand
content: Astronomical colour–colour diagrams (CCDs) are adapted to satellite observations to evaluate river turbidity as an indirect indicator of arsenic contamination in the Kok and Sai Rivers, northern Thailand. Six pseudo-colour indices and 15 candidate CCDs were constructed from four Sentinel-2 spectral bands at 10~m spatial resolution. Analysis of 296 paired ground-based measurements yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.735 for measured turbidity in discriminating arsenic exceedances in the Kok River. Uncertainties in sampling dates and locations limited the satellite-based analysis to 45 exploratory observations from the Kok River. Under nested leave-one-station-out cross-validation, the CCD models consistently selected visible-band colour indices and achieved a root mean square error of 0.271 on the logarithmic turbidity scale, compared with 0.337 for the baseline and 0.307 for the four-band model. The four-band model, however, performed better when entire monitoring rounds were withheld. Despite the improved turbidity estimation, CCD-estimated turbidity showed limited ability to discriminate arsenic exceedances (AUC = 0.494). These results warrant further evaluation of astronomical photometry for river turbidity assessment using concurrent satellite and field observations with verified sampling coordinates.
